findings.title: _source decryption builds the SavedObject from the raw ES `_id` and omits `namespace`, so the AAD never matches
findings.body: `rawId` is the Elasticsearch document `_id` from `METADATA _id`. For saved objects that value is the serialized raw id (`<type>:<id>`, or `<ns>:<type>:<id>` for single-namespace types outside the default space), not the saved object id. The reconstructed object also sets only `namespaces` and never `namespace`, which is what single-namespace types use for AAD. `decryptOrStripResponseAttributes` therefore rebuilds the AAD with the wrong descriptor, decryption fails, and encrypted attributes are always stripped. The documented "decrypted in `_source`, same as find/search" behaviour never works against real data; the unit test only passes because the extension is mocked. Fix: convert the raw id with the serializer (or `helpers.serializer.rawToSavedObject` on `{ _id, _source }`) so `id` and `namespace` are derived the same way `find` derives them.

findings.title: The agent's task-tracking files are committed to the repository
findings.body: `tasks/prd.json` and `tasks/progress.txt` are the work log and PRD of an autonomous agent run (branch `ralph/esql-search-saved-objects`, "Ralph Progress Log"). They are not part of the feature, are not under any package, and would leave stray top-level files in Kibana. They are also already stale: they describe a `@kbn/esql-language` tagged-template approach that the code and docs do not use. Remove both files from the PR.

findings.title: The pipeline is not required to start with `|`, so callers can extend the generated FROM clause
findings.body: The query is built as `${fromClause} ${pipeline}`, and the only validation rejects a pipeline that starts with FROM/ROW/SHOW/METRICS. A pipeline such as `, .some-other-index | LIMIT 100` (or one that adds its own METADATA list) is appended directly to `FROM <indices>`, adding indices that do not come from `getIndicesForTypes`. The query runs as `kibana_system`. The injected namespace/type `filter` still applies, but any document in another index that matches those fields can be read, which defeats the claim that index resolution is controlled by the system. Fix: require the trimmed pipeline to be empty or to start with `|`, e.g. `/^\s*(\|[\s\S]*)?$/`.

findings.title: Encrypted values leak when `_source` is returned without `_id`, or when columns are renamed or derived
findings.body: `decryptSourceColumn` returns the response unchanged when there is no `_id` column. So `metadata: ['_source']`, or a pipeline that drops `_id` (`| KEEP _source`), returns every `_source` document with its encrypted attributes as raw ciphertext; the unit test at line 410 even locks this in. `stripEncryptedColumns` only nulls columns whose name is exactly `<type>.<attr>`, so `| RENAME connector.secrets AS s`, `| EVAL s = connector.secrets` or `| STATS VALUES(connector.secrets)` also get past it. This contradicts the stated guarantee that encrypted attribute values are stripped. Fix: if `_source` is present without a usable `_id`, strip the encrypted attributes from `_source` instead of passing it through. Then either reject pipelines that reference encrypted attribute names, or document clearly that only exact column names are covered.
